channel.description: Anthropic Claude official blog / changelog in English (最近 50 条, 50 items). Generated by free-llm-intel.

item.title: We’ve launched Linked billing in beta with the user-profiles…
item.description: Full title: We’ve launched Linked billing in beta with the user-profiles-billing-2026-10-01 beta header.
item.content:encoded: • We’ve launched Linked billing in beta with the user-profiles-billing-2026-10-01 beta header. Your customers can now pay for the Claude usage in your app through their own Claude organization. Once a customer links their organization, set billing_policy on each /v1/messages or /v1/chat/completions request to choose who pays. In the Claude Console, customers can set a spend cap for your app or unlink your app. Linked billing works for customers whose organization pays Anthropic directly for API usage.

item.title: Text generated by Claude Opus 4.6, Claude Opus 4.5, Claude S…
item.description: Full title: Text generated by Claude Opus 4.6, Claude Opus 4.5, Claude Sonnet 4.5, and Claude Haiku 4.5 carries Anthropic’s text watermark on supported…
item.content:encoded: • Text generated by Claude Opus 4.6, Claude Opus 4.5, Claude Sonnet 4.5, and Claude Haiku 4.5 carries Anthropic’s text watermark on supported platforms. How Claude marks AI-generated content lists those platforms. If a request to one of these models sets temperature, top_p, or top_k to a non-default value, the text might not carry the watermark. See Text watermark.

item.title: We’ve added two event types to organization webhooks, which…
item.description: Full title: We’ve added two event types to organization webhooks, which are in beta.
item.content:encoded: • We’ve added two event types to organization webhooks, which are in beta. We send external_key.failed when your key management service keeps refusing a customer-managed encryption key, and external_key.recovered when the key works again.

item.title: We’ve launched self-hosted Claude Managed Agents.
item.content:encoded: • We’ve launched self-hosted Claude Managed Agents. You run the whole Managed Agents service, not only self-hosted sandboxes, on your own infrastructure, and you store agents, sessions, and session history there. The server sends model requests to the provider that you choose, which is Anthropic by default. To request access, contact your Anthropic account team.

item.title: We’ve launched Claude Fable 5.2 (claude-fable-5-2), built fo…
item.description: Full title: We’ve launched Claude Fable 5.2 (claude-fable-5-2), built for demanding reasoning and long-horizon agentic work.
item.content:encoded:
• We’ve launched Claude Fable 5.2 (claude-fable-5-2), built for demanding reasoning and long-horizon agentic work. Claude Mythos 5.2 (claude-mythos-5-2) offers the same capabilities only to organizations verified through Anthropic’s verification programs, such as the Cyber Verification Program. Both models have a 1M token context window, 128k max output tokens, and always-on adaptive thinking. They cost $8 USD per MTok of input and $40 USD per MTok of output (Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1 cost $10 USD per MTok of input and $50 USD per MTok of output). Claude Fable 5.2 is available on the Claude API, Amazon Bedrock (bedrock-runtime), Claude Platform on AWS, Claude Models on Google Cloud (Anthropic managed), Claude Models on Google Cloud (Google managed), and Claude in Microsoft Foundry. See What’s new in Claude Fable 5.2 for API changes and migration guidance. For model-specific prompting patterns, see Prompting Claude Fable 5.2.
  • Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 enforce the prefix check for every account, whatever its age. Claude Fable 5.1 returns the error by default on accounts created on or after August 31, 2026 (see When prefix_mismatch_behavior is unset). If your code edits the system prompt, tools, or an earlier message and then sends back a Claude Fable 5.2 or Claude Mythos 5.2 thinking block from a later turn, the request returns a 400 error. Before you switch, check whether your code edits the prefix.
  • Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 read other models’ thinking blocks on the Claude API and Claude Models on Google Cloud (Google managed). So on those platforms, a conversation that moves onto either model keeps its reasoning. The other models include Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5, and Claude Haiku 5.5.
  • No other model reads thinking blocks from Claude Fable 5.2 or Claude Mythos 5.2. When a conversation moves from either one to a model outside this pair, the API drops those blocks. That includes a move to Claude Opus 5.5 or Claude Fable 5.1. The request still succeeds. See Switching models mid-conversation.
  • Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 support computer use through the computer_toolset_20260801 toolset. A request that declares the earlier computer_20251124 tool returns a 400 error on every platform except Amazon Bedrock, where the earlier tool still works. See Migrate from computer_20251124.
  • With the advisor tool, which is in beta, a Claude Fable 5.2 or Claude Mythos 5.2 executor accepts only Claude Fable 5.2 or Claude Mythos 5.2 as its advisor. Any other advisor returns a 400 error, so set the advisor’s model to one of these two models when you move an executor to them. Every executor model accepts Claude Fable 5.2 as its advisor. See Model compatibility.
  • Both models require 30-day data retention, like Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1. They aren’t available under zero data retention unless expressly authorized by Anthropic. See Model-specific data retention requirements.
  • Thinking blocks that Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 produce work only in the account that produced them, or in an account linked to it. See Preserved thinking.

item.title: Dreams (research preview) now supports Claude Fable 5.2.
item.content:encoded: • Dreams (research preview) now supports Claude Fable 5.2. See Supported models.

item.title: We’ve launched fast mode for Claude Fable 5.2 in Messages AP…
item.description: Full title: We’ve launched fast mode for Claude Fable 5.2 in Messages API requests on the Claude API.
item.content:encoded: • We’ve launched fast mode for Claude Fable 5.2 in Messages API requests on the Claude API. Fast mode delivers up to 2.5x higher output tokens per second, at $16 USD per MTok of input and $80 USD per MTok of output. Set speed: "fast" on your request, with no beta header.

item.title: The Compliance API now includes Security posture data, in be…
item.description: Full title: The Compliance API now includes Security posture data, in beta for Claude Enterprise organizations.
item.content:encoded: • The Compliance API now includes Security posture data, in beta for Claude Enterprise organizations. The Activity Feed records changes to attestations on the Security posture page in claude.ai Organization settings. The GET /v1/compliance/organizations/{organization_id}/security_posture endpoint returns an organization’s current Security posture results. See Security posture in the Compliance API.

item.title: You can now set up an IP allowlist for your organization in…
item.description: Full title: You can now set up an IP allowlist for your organization in the Claude Console, in beta.
item.content:encoded: • You can now set up an IP allowlist for your organization in the Claude Console, in beta. Requests to covered services from addresses not on your list are refused, which limits where a leaked API key can be used. Add IPv4 and IPv6 addresses or CIDR ranges, up to 1,000 per organization. See IP allowlisting for what’s covered and how to set it up.

item.title: You can now sign a member of your Claude Enterprise (claude.…
item.description: Full title: You can now sign a member of your Claude Enterprise (claude.ai) organization out of Claude everywhere with the Admin API.
item.content:encoded: • You can now sign a member of your Claude Enterprise (claude.ai) organization out of Claude everywhere with the Admin API. This capability is in beta. See the Admin API reference. The member stays in the organization and can sign in again. See Sign a member out everywhere for the beta header and what the request doesn’t end.

item.title: Text generated by Claude Mythos 5, Claude Opus 4.7, and Clau…
item.description: Full title: Text generated by Claude Mythos 5, Claude Opus 4.7, and Claude Sonnet 4.6 carries Anthropic’s text watermark on the platforms listed in How…
item.content:encoded: • Text generated by Claude Mythos 5, Claude Opus 4.7, and Claude Sonnet 4.6 carries Anthropic’s text watermark on the platforms listed in How Claude marks AI-generated content. On Claude Sonnet 4.6, text generated for a request that sets temperature, top_p, or top_k to a non-default value might not carry it. See Text watermark.

item.title: Long conversations and agent loops on the Messages API can n…
item.description: Full title: Long conversations and agent loops on the Messages API can now send smaller requests and get a lower time to first token with message…
item.content:encoded: • Long conversations and agent loops on the Messages API can now send smaller requests and get a lower time to first token with message threads, in beta with the message-threads-2026-08-12 beta header. The API keeps the conversation on the server, so each later request sends only the new messages. A thread expires 5 minutes after its last request and is deleted no more than 1 hour after its last use. Message threads are available on the Claude API, Claude Platform on AWS, Claude Models on Google Cloud (Anthropic managed), and Claude in Microsoft Foundry.

item.title: We’ve deprecated fast mode for Claude Opus 4.8, with removal…
item.description: Full title: We’ve deprecated fast mode for Claude Opus 4.8, with removal on November 30, 2026.
item.content:encoded: • We’ve deprecated fast mode for Claude Opus 4.8, with removal on November 30, 2026. After removal, requests to claude-opus-4-8 with speed: "fast" will return an error. To continue using fast mode, migrate to Claude Opus 5.5. Read more in Fast mode model availability.

item.title: We’ve launched the Usage and Cost Analytics API in beta with…
item.description: Full title: We’ve launched the Usage and Cost Analytics API in beta with the analytics-usage-cost-2026-08-24 beta header.
item.content:encoded:
• We’ve launched the Usage and Cost Analytics API in beta with the analytics-usage-cost-2026-08-24 beta header. Its /v1/organizations/analytics/usage and /v1/organizations/analytics/cost endpoints report token usage and cost for Claude Console and Claude Enterprise organizations. You can filter and group results by dimensions such as model, workspace, API key, and the user or service account behind each request.
  • The Usage and Cost API is now a legacy API, and so are the usage_report, cost_report, user_usage_report, and user_cost_report endpoints of the Claude Enterprise Analytics API. All of them remain supported. To move an existing integration, see Migrate from the Usage and Cost API or Migrate from the Claude Enterprise usage and cost reports.

item.title: We’ve raised the maximum request size for the Messages API a…
item.description: Full title: We’ve raised the maximum request size for the Messages API and the Token Counting API from 32 MB to 128 MB on the first-party Claude API.
item.content:encoded: • We’ve raised the maximum request size for the Messages API and the Token Counting API from 32 MB to 128 MB on the first-party Claude API.

item.title: The Claude Tag API is available in beta for Claude Enterpris…
item.description: Full title: The Claude Tag API is available in beta for Claude Enterprise organizations with the experimental-claude-tag-2026-10-21 beta header.
item.content:encoded: • The Claude Tag API is available in beta for Claude Enterprise organizations with the experimental-claude-tag-2026-10-21 beta header. Its /v1/organizations/claude_tag/ endpoints read and change Claude Tag settings on Slack channels and Slack workspaces, show which settings apply in a channel and where each comes from, and attach Access bundles. Call it with an Admin API key that your primary owner creates in claude.ai with the read:claude_tag or write:claude_tag scope. It is not available to Claude Platform (Claude Console) organizations.

item.title: We’ve launched Claude Models on Google Cloud (Anthropic mana…
item.description: Full title: We’ve launched Claude Models on Google Cloud (Anthropic managed), the Claude API operated by Anthropic and reached through your Google Cloud…
item.content:encoded:
• We’ve launched Claude Models on Google Cloud (Anthropic managed), the Claude API operated by Anthropic and reached through your Google Cloud project. Google Cloud IAM controls access. Google Cloud Marketplace handles billing.
  • Fast mode is available for Claude Opus 5.5 on Claude Models on Google Cloud (Anthropic managed).

item.title: We’ve released API version 2026-10-21.
item.content:encoded:
• We’ve released API version 2026-10-21. Migrating to API version 2026-10-21 shows how to upgrade.
  • We’ve released new versions of the client SDKs and the ant CLI that send API version 2026-10-21 by default: Python SDK 2.0.0, TypeScript SDK 1.0.0, C# SDK 13.0.0, Go SDK 2.0.0, Java SDK 3.0.0, PHP SDK 1.0.0, Ruby SDK 2.0.0, and ant CLI 2.0.0. See Switch to 2026-10-21.
  • The new SDK and CLI versions also have breaking changes that don’t depend on the API version, and they are licensed under Apache 2.0 instead of the MIT License. See SDK and CLI changes.
  • We’ve added the enforcement_status and enforcement_actions fields to user profiles, so you can see whether Anthropic has restricted or banned one of your end customers. To find the profiles that have an open restriction or ban, list your profiles with the new enforcement_status[] filter. See Check whether Anthropic has restricted or banned a profile.

item.title: Inference hooks are out of beta for Claude Enterprise organi…
item.description: Full title: Inference hooks are out of beta for Claude Enterprise organizations.
item.content:encoded:
• Inference hooks are out of beta for Claude Enterprise organizations.
  • We’ve launched user profiles, so you can tell Anthropic which of your end customers each API request is for. If you operate a platform or gateway, or resell API access, a safety enforcement action can then apply to one end customer instead of your whole organization. The SDK and the ant CLI support the new /v1/user_profiles endpoints.
  • We’ve added organization webhooks to the Admin API, in beta with the webhooks-2026-10-07 beta header. Its /v1/organizations/webhooks endpoints register webhook endpoints for two event types: one for when Anthropic restricts or bans one of your organization’s user profiles, and one for when the restriction or ban ends. To request access, contact your Anthropic account team.
  • Organization admins can now turn off web fetch for their organization on the Capabilities page of the Claude Console. With web fetch off, a Messages API request that includes the web fetch tool fails with a 400 error. In a Claude Managed Agents session, web_fetch calls return an error result to the agent instead. With web fetch on, admins can also set allowed or blocked domains for web fetch on the same page. See How to use web fetch and Domain filtering.
  • In Claude Managed Agents, the web_fetch tool now follows your organization’s web fetch domain restrictions set on the Capabilities page of the Claude Console. A URL, including one reached by a redirect, must pass both the organization’s list and the allowed_domains or blocked_domains list on the agent’s web_fetch tool. See Restrict web search and web fetch domains.
  • In Claude Managed Agents, sessions follow your organization’s web search settings on the Capabilities page of the Claude Console: the Allow web search setting since October 6, and its web search domain restrictions since October 14. The agent receives only the search results that both the organization’s domain restrictions and the allowed_domains or blocked_domains list on the agent’s web_search tool allow. See Restrict web search and web fetch domains.

item.title: We’ve added capabilities.thinking.types.between_tools to the…
item.description: Full title: We’ve added capabilities.thinking.types.between_tools to the Models API.
item.content:encoded:
• We’ve added capabilities.thinking.types.between_tools to the Models API. GET /v1/models and GET /v1/models/{model_id} now report whether each model accepts thinking: {type: "between_tools"}, which turns off up-front thinking. See Using the Models API.
  • The Compliance API now returns the text each organization member saved as Instructions for Claude in claude.ai and as Global instructions in Cowork, in beta for Claude Enterprise organizations. Call GET /v1/compliance/organizations/{org_uuid}/user_preferences with your existing Compliance Access Key and the read:compliance_user_data scope. See List user preferences.
  • Fast mode is out of research preview for Claude Opus 5.5, and you no longer need to request access. Requests to Claude Opus 5.5 no longer require the fast-mode-2026-02-01 beta header, and requests that still send it keep working. Claude Opus 5.5 now has a default fast mode rate limit in the Start, Build, and Scale usage tiers. Fast mode for Claude Opus 5 and Claude Opus 4.8 remains in research preview. Keep sending the beta header with fast mode requests to those models.
  • Fast mode for Claude Opus 5.5 is now available on Claude in Microsoft Foundry for deployments hosted on Azure.

item.title: We’ve launched OpenTelemetry export in beta, so you can trac…
item.description: Full title: We’ve launched OpenTelemetry export in beta, so you can trace Messages API requests and Claude Managed Agents sessions in your observability…
item.content:encoded:
• We’ve launched OpenTelemetry export in beta, so you can trace Messages API requests and Claude Managed Agents sessions in your observability platform. The Claude SDK emits spans in Python, TypeScript, C#, Go, Java, PHP, and Ruby. To get spans from the API, add an OpenTelemetry destination in the Claude Console.
  • Claude Managed Agents scheduled deployments are now available on Claude Platform on AWS.

item.title: You can now let a Claude Managed Agents agent use dynamic wo…
item.description: Full title: You can now let a Claude Managed Agents agent use dynamic workflows, in beta with the managed-agents-2026-04-01 beta header.
item.content:encoded: • You can now let a Claude Managed Agents agent use dynamic workflows, in beta with the managed-agents-2026-04-01 beta header. For work with many pieces, such as reviewing hundreds of documents, the agent can write a workflow. A workflow is a program that runs many agents in phases and combines their results. The server runs it in the background as a workflow run. To turn dynamic workflows on, set the agent’s multiagent field to {"type": "multiagent_20261001", "workflows": {"type": "enabled"}}. To guide the agent, tell it in its system prompt when to start a run. Follow each run through workflow_run.* events on the session’s event stream. See Workflow runs.

item.title: The Compliance API chat endpoints now also return chats from…
item.description: Full title: The Compliance API chat endpoints now also return chats from the unified Claude experience, in beta for Claude Enterprise organizations, with…
item.content:encoded:
• The Compliance API chat endpoints now also return chats from the unified Claude experience, in beta for Claude Enterprise organizations, with your existing Compliance Access Key. See Retrieve and delete chats, files, and projects.
  • The Compliance API can now download Claude Docs documents as Word files, in beta. See Retrieve files and artifacts.

item.title: We’ve lowered the price of prompt cache reads on Claude Sonn…
item.description: Full title: We’ve lowered the price of prompt cache reads on Claude Sonnet 5.5 from $0.20 USD to $0.10 USD per million tokens: 0.05x the base input price…
item.content:encoded:
• We’ve lowered the price of prompt cache reads on Claude Sonnet 5.5 from $0.20 USD to $0.10 USD per million tokens: 0.05x the base input price instead of 0.1x. Cache writes and all other prices are unchanged. See Prompt caching pricing.
  • We’ve launched Claude Haiku 5.5 (claude-haiku-5-5), our most capable model tuned for high-volume and latency-sensitive work. It has a 1M token context window, 128k max output tokens, and adaptive thinking with the effort parameter. It’s available on the Claude API, Claude in Amazon Bedrock, Claude Platform on AWS, Claude Models on Google Cloud (Google managed), and Claude in Microsoft Foundry. See What’s new in Claude Haiku 5.5.
  • Code written for Claude Haiku 4.5 can break on Claude Haiku 5.5. Manual extended thinking (budget_tokens), the sampling parameters temperature, top_p, and top_k, and assistant message prefill can each return a 400 error. computer_20250124 also returns a 400 error: use the computer_toolset_20260801 toolset on the Claude API and Google Cloud, or computer_20251124 on Amazon Bedrock. A request that sends thinking blocks back after a change to system, tools, or earlier turns can also return a 400 error. Adaptive thinking is on by default, so a response can begin with thinking blocks, and their text is omitted unless you set thinking.display to "summarized". Claude Haiku 5.5 also uses a tokenizer that produces more tokens for the same text. See the Claude Haiku 5.5 migration guide for each change. For model-specific prompting patterns, see Prompting Claude Haiku 5.5.
  • Python SDK 1.12.0 and TypeScript SDK 0.132.0 add classes, in beta, for the browser use tool and the computer use tool. You subclass one and write one method per tool against your own browser or desktop automation. The SDK runs the tool loop, the URL and file policies you set for the browser, and your approval callback. See Browser and computer use with the SDK toolsets.
  • Claude Max, Ultra, and Team plans now include monthly API credits. To learn how to claim them, see API credits for Max, Ultra, and Team plans.
  • In Claude Managed Agents, a cloud environment with limited networking now also applies its allowed_hosts to the web_search and web_fetch tools. A web_fetch call for a URL on a host that allowed_hosts does not match returns a url_not_allowed error result to the agent. web_search omits results from such hosts. When allowed_hosts lists no hosts, neither tool returns a page or a search result. allow_package_managers and allow_mcp_servers add no hosts for these tools. To let the tools reach a host, add it to allowed_hosts, which also opens it to the sandbox. unrestricted networking and self-hosted environments do not limit these tools. See Environment networking.
  • With limited networking, creating a session fails with a 400 error when an enabled web tool’s allowed_domains has an entry not within allowed_hosts. So does a session update that adds such an entry. An allowed_hosts entry matches one exact host unless it starts with *., so docs.example.com is not within ["example.com"]. To fix the error, add the host to allowed_hosts or remove the entry from allowed_domains. See Restrict web search and web fetch domains.
  • In Claude Managed Agents, the web_fetch tool now fetches only URLs that have already appeared in the session, for example in the text of a user message, in a web_search result, or in a page that web_fetch returned earlier. This reduces the risk of data exfiltration. A URL that appears only in Claude’s own output, the agent’s system prompt, an attached document, or the output of a tool such as bash, read, or an MCP tool does not count: a web_fetch call for it returns a url_not_in_prior_context error result to the agent. To let the agent fetch a URL, send it in the text of a user.message event.

item.title: We’ve added capabilities.server_tools to the Models API.
item.content:encoded: • We’ve added capabilities.server_tools to the Models API. GET /v1/models and GET /v1/models/{model_id} now report whether each model accepts the web search and code execution tools. To check whether a model accepts the code execution tool, read capabilities.server_tools.code_execution. The top-level capabilities.code_execution reports whether code can call your request’s other tools. See Using the Models API.

item.title: We’ve added capabilities.thinking.types.disabled to the Mode…
item.description: Full title: We’ve added capabilities.thinking.types.disabled to the Models API.
item.content:encoded: • We’ve added capabilities.thinking.types.disabled to the Models API. GET /v1/models and GET /v1/models/{model_id} now report whether each model accepts thinking: {type: "disabled"}, which turns thinking off. See Using the Models API.

item.title: We’ve added a line field to the Models API.
item.content:encoded:
• We’ve added a line field to the Models API. GET /v1/models and GET /v1/models/{model_id} now return the model line each model belongs to. Claude Opus 4.5 and Claude Opus 4.6 both report opus, for example. Use line to group models without parsing their IDs. line is null for a model that belongs to no line. See Using the Models API.
  • Dreams (research preview) now supports Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Fable 5.1, and Claude Sonnet 5.5. See Supported models.

item.title: In Python SDK 1.10.0, TypeScript SDK 0.130.0, C# SDK 12.52.0…
item.description: Full title: In Python SDK 1.10.0, TypeScript SDK 0.130.0, C# SDK 12.52.0, Go SDK 1.77.0, Java SDK 2.67.0, PHP SDK 0.53.0, Ruby SDK 1.75.0, and version…
item.content:encoded:
• In Python SDK 1.10.0, TypeScript SDK 0.130.0, C# SDK 12.52.0, Go SDK 1.77.0, Java SDK 2.67.0, PHP SDK 0.53.0, Ruby SDK 1.75.0, and version 1.37.0 of the ant CLI, the Admin API methods for organization info, members, invites, workspaces, API keys, rate limits, service accounts, workload identity federation, customer-managed encryption keys, and compliance settings are out of beta: call them under client.organization and ant organization. These releases also keep client.beta.organization and ant beta:organization.
  • We announced the deprecation of the Claude Sonnet 4.5 model (claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929), with retirement on the Claude API scheduled for November 30, 2026. We recommend migrating to Claude Sonnet 5.5. Read more in Model deprecations.

item.title: We’ve launched Claude Sonnet 5.5 (claude-sonnet-5-5).
item.content:encoded:
• We’ve launched Claude Sonnet 5.5 (claude-sonnet-5-5). It’s available on the Claude API, Claude in Amazon Bedrock, Claude Platform on AWS, Claude Models on Google Cloud (Google managed), and Claude in Microsoft Foundry. For its context window, output limits, and prices, see the Claude Sonnet 5.5 model page.
  • Code written for Claude Sonnet 5 can break on Claude Sonnet 5.5 in five ways. To turn off up-front thinking, send thinking: {"type": "between_tools"} instead of "disabled", at high effort or below. Forced tool use (tool_choice types any and tool) returns a 400 error. Thinking blocks are tied to the model and the conversation. On the Claude API and Google Cloud, the earlier computer_20251124 computer use tool isn’t accepted. The advisor tool rejects Claude Opus 4.8, Claude Opus 4.7, and Claude Sonnet 5 as advisors. See What’s new in Claude Sonnet 5.5 for each change and the Claude Sonnet 5.5 migration guide for before-and-after requests. For model-specific prompting patterns, see Prompting Claude Sonnet 5.5.
  • Thinking blocks that Claude Sonnet 5.5 produces work only in the account that produced them, or in an account linked to it. When another account sends one of these blocks, the API drops the block before the model sees it, and the request succeeds. Blocks from earlier models aren’t affected. See Thinking blocks stay with the account that produced them.

item.title: We’re resuming billing for refusals that arrive before any o…
item.description: Full title: We’re resuming billing for refusals that arrive before any output when stop_details.category is "bio", "frontier_llm", or…
item.content:encoded:
• We’re resuming billing for refusals that arrive before any output when stop_details.category is "bio", "frontier_llm", or "reasoning_extraction", the categories where we measure low volumes of false positives. Mid-stream refusals were already billed. Refusals billed under this change are charged like any other request, at the rates of the model that ran it. Refusals before any output in other categories are still not billed, and fallback credit is unchanged. This change applies on all platforms. See How refusals are billed.
  • The Compliance API local session endpoints are out of beta for Claude for Microsoft 365 sessions in Excel, PowerPoint, Word, and Outlook (product_surface values beginning with office_agents). See Sessions on users’ machines.
  • The Compliance API Activity Feed no longer returns file names, project document names, or artifact titles. The filename and title fields on file, project document, and artifact activities are now always empty or omitted, including on activities recorded before this change. To look up a name or title by the ID on the activity, use a Compliance Access Key with the read:compliance_user_data scope. See Understand the Activity object.

item.title: Cache diagnostics is out of beta on the Claude API and no lo…
item.description: Full title: Cache diagnostics is out of beta on the Claude API and no longer requires the cache-diagnosis-2026-04-07 beta header.
item.content:encoded: • Cache diagnostics is out of beta on the Claude API and no longer requires the cache-diagnosis-2026-04-07 beta header. Include the diagnostics object on a Messages request to opt in; requests that still send the header work as before. Responses from POST /v1/messages now always include the diagnostics field, which is null when the request did not include the diagnostics object.

item.title: We’ve launched Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5), a model fo…
item.description: Full title: We’ve launched Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5), a model for long-running agentic coding and knowledge work.
item.content:encoded:
• We’ve launched Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5), a model for long-running agentic coding and knowledge work. It has a 1M token context window by default, 128k max output tokens, and always-on adaptive thinking, at $4 / $20 USD per MTok (Claude Opus 5 is $5 / $25 USD). Claude Opus 5.5 is available on the Claude API, Claude in Amazon Bedrock, Claude Platform on AWS, Claude Models on Google Cloud (Google managed), and Claude in Microsoft Foundry. See What’s new in Claude Opus 5.5 for capabilities, API changes, and migration guidance.
  • On Claude Opus 5.5, thinking can’t be disabled: thinking: {"type": "disabled"} and thinking: {"type": "enabled", ...} return a 400 error. Omit the thinking field and control thinking depth with the effort parameter. tool_choice types any and tool also return a 400 error, as on Claude Fable 5.1; use auto with strict tool use. On the Claude API and Google Cloud, computer use on this model requires the computer_toolset_20260801 toolset and the earlier computer_20251124 tool returns a 400 error; on Amazon Bedrock, computer_20251124 keeps working. See the Claude Opus 5.5 migration guide.
  • Fast mode (research preview) is available for Claude Opus 5.5 on the Claude API.
  • Tools can now be defined inside a mid-conversation system message, in beta on the Claude API with the inline-tools-2026-09-15 beta header. A tool_addition block can carry the tool’s full definition (tool: {"type": "tool_definition", "definition": {...}}), so you can add a tool, change its schema, or move a server tool to a newer version without editing tools or invalidating the prompt cache. The same header covers adding and removing tools by reference. With the MCP connector’s mcp-client-2026-09-15 beta header as well, the definition can be an MCP toolset, and a response records each server’s fetched tool list in an mcp_tool_listing block, which pins that list when you send it back.

item.title: For cache diagnostics, a response to a request that sends th…
item.description: Full title: For cache diagnostics, a response to a request that sends the cache-diagnosis-2026-04-07 beta header now always includes the diagnostics field.
item.content:encoded:
• For cache diagnostics, a response to a request that sends the cache-diagnosis-2026-04-07 beta header now always includes the diagnostics field. The field is null when the request did not include the diagnostics object. Previously the field was omitted in that case.
  • The Compliance API local session endpoints now also return transcripts of Claude in Chrome sessions (product_surface value claude_in_chrome), in beta for Claude Enterprise organizations, with your existing Compliance Access Key and the read:compliance_user_data scope. See Sessions on users’ machines.

item.title: The Messages API can now compact a conversation on demand on…
item.description: Full title: The Messages API can now compact a conversation on demand on the Claude API, in beta with the compact-2026-09-04 beta header.
item.content:encoded:
• The Messages API can now compact a conversation on demand on the Claude API, in beta with the compact-2026-09-04 beta header. Send the top-level compaction parameter, and the API returns a signed compaction block that summarizes the messages you sent. On later requests, send that block first, in place of those messages. You choose when to compact, the request can run in the background, and you can keep recent turns word for word after the summary. On models with preserved thinking, the thinking in those kept turns can stay valid.
  • With the thinking-binding-controls-2026-08-01 beta header, the input_transformations response field gains a second entry type, thinking_mismatch_allowed. It names a thinking block that failed the prefix check on a request where the API doesn’t enforce that check: on Claude Fable 5.1, for example, a request from an account created before August 31, 2026, with prefix_mismatch_behavior unset. The block still reaches the model unchanged. Log these entries to find history edits in production traffic before you opt into enforcement. See Set the mismatch behavior and read input_transformations.

item.title: Claude Managed Agents permission policies now include auto:…
item.description: Full title: Claude Managed Agents permission policies now include auto: the server evaluates each agent or MCP tool call and runs it, denies it, or…
item.content:encoded:
• Claude Managed Agents permission policies now include auto: the server evaluates each agent or MCP tool call and runs it, denies it, or pauses for your approval. agent.tool_use and agent.mcp_tool_use events report how each call was evaluated in an evaluation field alongside evaluated_permission. See Let the server evaluate each call with auto.
  • Version 1.32.0 of the ant CLI adds ant beta:sessions connect, which attaches your terminal to a Claude Managed Agents session. You can follow the session live, send messages, and allow or deny tool calls that are waiting for approval. Pass --web to serve the Claude Console’s session viewer locally and open the session there instead. See Connect to a Managed Agents session from your terminal.

item.title: For cache diagnostics, the API now stores a request’s finger…
item.description: Full title: For cache diagnostics, the API now stores a request’s fingerprint only when the request includes the diagnostics object.
item.content:encoded: • For cache diagnostics, the API now stores a request’s fingerprint only when the request includes the diagnostics object. A request that sends only the cache-diagnosis-2026-04-07 beta header is still accepted, but no fingerprint is stored. A later turn that points previous_message_id at it reports previous_message_not_found. Include diagnostics on every turn, with "previous_message_id": null on the first.

item.title: Version 1.30.0 of the ant CLI adds ant apply, which creates…
item.description: Full title: Version 1.30.0 of the ant CLI adds ant apply, which creates and updates agents, environments, skills, memory stores, and deployments from…
item.content:encoded:
• Version 1.30.0 of the ant CLI adds ant apply, which creates and updates agents, environments, skills, memory stores, and deployments from files in your repository. Describe each resource in a file, run ant apply, and approve the plan it prints. Commit the claude-lock.json lockfile it writes so that later runs, on your machine or in CI, update the same resources instead of creating new ones. See Manage resources as code with ant apply.
  • Per-message effort changes, in beta, are also available on Google Cloud for Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Mythos 5.1, and Claude Opus 5, with the same mid-conversation-output-config-2026-07-01 beta header.

item.title: We’ve launched Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), the succ…
item.description: Full title: We’ve launched Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), the successor to Claude Fable 5 for long-running agentic coding, knowledge work, and…
item.content:encoded:
• We’ve launched Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), the successor to Claude Fable 5 for long-running agentic coding, knowledge work, and research. For Project Glasswing participants, we’ve also launched Claude Mythos 5.1 (claude-mythos-5-1). Both models support a 1M token context window by default, 128k max output tokens, and always-on adaptive thinking. They cost $10 / $50 USD per MTok, the same as Claude Fable 5, with cache reads cut to $0.25 USD per MTok. Claude Fable 5.1 is available on the Claude API, Claude in Amazon Bedrock, and Claude Platform on AWS. It’s also on Claude Models on Google Cloud (Google managed) and Claude in Microsoft Foundry. See Claude Fable 5.1 for specifications.
  • Prompt cache reads on Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1 cost $0.25 USD per million tokens: 0.025x the base input price, compared with 0.1x on other models. Cache writes are unchanged. See Prompt caching pricing.
  • On Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1, tool_choice types any and tool aren’t supported and return a 400 error. auto and none are unchanged. To guarantee schema-conformant tool inputs, use strict tool use or structured outputs.
  • Thinking blocks produced by Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1 are preserved only for the model that produced them or a newer one: earlier models can’t read them, and the API drops one replayed to an earlier model. Claude Fable 5.1 accepts thinking blocks from Claude Opus 5, Claude Fable 5, Claude Mythos 5, and earlier Claude models. On Claude Fable 5.1, the API also checks that nothing before a block has changed: for new accounts created on or after August 31, 2026, replaying one after the system prompt, tools, or an earlier message changed returns a 400 error. With the thinking-binding-controls-2026-08-01 beta header, dropped blocks are reported in an input_transformations response field, and thinking.block_binding.prefix_mismatch_behavior chooses between rejecting and dropping blocks whose history changed. See Preserved thinking.
  • Per-message effort changes are in beta on Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Mythos 5.1, and Claude Opus 5 on the Claude API. Add a role: "system" message with output_config.effort inside messages to change effort for later turns while preserving the prompt cache. Include the mid-conversation-output-config-2026-07-01 beta header in your requests. See Per-message effort.
  • Turn-scoped system messages are in beta (mid-conversation-system-clear-at-2026-08-21 header). Set clear_at: "next_user_message" on a mid-conversation role: "system" message and it renders for the current turn only, then stays in the history at no token cost. Per-turn reminders don’t accumulate and don’t invalidate the prompt cache or later thinking blocks.
  • thinking.display accepts a third value, "updates", in beta (thinking-display-updates-2026-08-18 header). Reasoning comes back with an empty thinking field, as under "omitted", and the short progress updates that Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Mythos 5.1, and Claude Fable 5 write between tool calls come back as text, at most one thinking block before a tool call. See Progress updates between tool calls.
  • Text generated by Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1 carries Anthropic’s text watermark, and supported image, video, and audio files that Claude produces through the code execution tool carry C2PA Content Credentials when you retrieve them through the Files API on the Claude API. Marking requires no changes to your requests or response handling.
  • Like Claude Fable 5, both models require 30-day data retention and aren’t available under zero data retention unless expressly authorized by Anthropic. See Model-specific data retention requirements.
  • The guides for the Claude Enterprise endpoints of the Admin API (user management and spend limits), the Claude Enterprise Analytics API, and the Compliance API now show the anthropic-version header; send it on every request to these endpoints, as in the rest of the Claude API. See API versions.

item.title: In Python SDK 1.2.0, TypeScript SDK 0.122.0, Go SDK 1.68.0,…
item.description: Full title: In Python SDK 1.2.0, TypeScript SDK 0.122.0, Go SDK 1.68.0, Java SDK 2.59.0, Ruby SDK 1.67.0, and C# SDK 12.44.0, client.beta.files and…
item.content:encoded:
• In Python SDK 1.2.0, TypeScript SDK 0.122.0, Go SDK 1.68.0, Java SDK 2.59.0, Ruby SDK 1.67.0, and C# SDK 12.44.0, client.beta.files and client.beta.skills no longer send the files-api-2025-04-14 and skills-2025-10-02 beta headers and return the same shapes as client.files and client.skills. With this change, client.beta.skills.delete() deletes a Skill together with all of its versions, and the beta Messages type BetaSkill (the container Skill reference) is renamed BetaContainerSkill. Requests that still send the beta headers keep receiving the beta shapes. See Migrate from files-api-2025-04-14 and Migrate from skills-2025-10-02.
  • You can now create personal keys and service account keys in the Claude Console. They act as you or as a service account, with the same permissions, and stop working when the linked account is removed from an organization. This lets organization admins more easily track usage for each account, and ensure key usage is legitimate. These API keys can be scoped to a specific workspace or work on admin endpoints and across any workspace the account has access to. Workspace API keys remain supported as a legacy option. See API keys in Authentication for more information.

item.title: The Compliance API session endpoints are out of beta for Cow…
item.description: Full title: The Compliance API session endpoints are out of beta for Cowork and Claude Code sessions.
item.content:encoded:
• The Compliance API session endpoints are out of beta for Cowork and Claude Code sessions. See Retrieve session transcripts.
  • The Compliance API local session endpoints now also return transcripts of Claude Science sessions (product_surface value claude_science) and Claude for Microsoft 365 sessions in Excel, PowerPoint, Word, and Outlook (product_surface values beginning with office_agents), in beta for Claude Enterprise organizations, with your existing Compliance Access Key and the read:compliance_user_data scope. See Sessions on users’ machines.
  • The Admin API is now available in the ant CLI and the Python, TypeScript, C#, Go, Java, PHP, and Ruby SDKs under client.beta.organization. They cover organization info, members, invites, workspaces and workspace members, API keys, rate limits, service accounts, workload identity federation issuers and rules, and customer-managed encryption keys. Usage and cost reports and the Claude Enterprise user-management and analytics endpoints remain curl-only. The CLI and SDKs read an Admin API key from ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or an org:admin OAuth token from ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN.

item.title: We’ve released v1.0 of the Python SDK.
item.content:encoded:
• We’ve released v1.0 of the Python SDK. The SDK’s HTTP layer moves from httpx to httpx2, a maintained, API-compatible fork: build custom http_client, Timeout, and transport objects from httpx2 (the DefaultHttpxClient helpers are unchanged), and call httpx2.alias_httpx() at startup if you rely on tracing or mocking libraries that patch httpx. v1.0 requires Python 3.10 or later and removes long-deprecated surface, including the legacy Text Completions API, the temperature, top_p, and top_k parameters on Messages methods, and the tool runner’s client-side compaction_control. On the async client, .with_raw_response results now need await response.parse(), and AnthropicBedrock now raises an error when no AWS region is configured instead of defaulting to us-east-1. See the v1 migration guide for every change with before-and-after snippets.
  • The computer use and browser use toolsets (computer_toolset_20260801 and browser_toolset_20260801) are now available on Google Cloud for Claude Fable 5, Claude Mythos 5, Claude Opus 5, Claude Sonnet 5, and Claude Opus 4.8. Requests use the same tools entries as on the Claude API.

item.title: The computer use tool is out of beta on the Claude API as th…
item.description: Full title: The computer use tool is out of beta on the Claude API as the computer_toolset_20260801 toolset: no beta header, batch actions (several…
item.content:encoded:
• The computer use tool is out of beta on the Claude API as the computer_toolset_20260801 toolset: no beta header, batch actions (several actions in one turn), zoom enabled by default, and per-member configuration through configs. Earlier beta versions remain available. Upgrading an existing integration changes the request shape and tool handling; see Migrate from computer_20251124.
  • We’ve launched the browser use tool (browser_toolset_20260801), a client toolset for driving a browser that your application hosts. It works inside a browser viewport rather than a whole desktop, reading the page itself (its accessibility tree, elements, forms, and tabs) and adding element references, form input, tab management, download reporting, and opt-in file upload on top of screenshot-and-click control.
  • Both toolsets are available for Claude Fable 5, Claude Mythos 5, Claude Opus 5, Claude Sonnet 5, and Claude Opus 4.8 on the Claude API.
  • The Files API is out of beta on the Claude API. Requests to the /v1/files endpoints, and Messages API requests that reference an uploaded file, no longer require the files-api-2025-04-14 beta header. Requests sent without the header use the current response format: file expiration (set expires_in_seconds when you upload a file; file objects report expires_at), and page and next_page pagination plus an ids[] filter when you list files. /v1/files requests that still send the beta header keep working and return the previous response format. To move an existing integration off the header, see Migrate from files-api-2025-04-14.
  • Agent Skills and the Skills API (/v1/skills) are out of beta on the Claude API. Requests no longer require the skills-2025-10-02 beta header, including Messages API requests that load Skills through the container parameter. Requests that still send the header continue to work unchanged. See Using Agent Skills with the API. To move an existing integration off the header, see Migrate from skills-2025-10-02.
  • The Admin API user-management endpoints for Claude Enterprise (claude.ai) organizations (members, invites, groups, and custom roles) are out of beta. The anthropic-beta: ce-user-management-2026-07-13 header is no longer required on group and custom-role requests; requests that still send it are accepted unchanged. See User management.
  • You can now restrict which sites a Claude Managed Agents agent’s web_search and web_fetch tools can reach. Set allowed_domains or blocked_domains on the tool’s entry in the agent_toolset_20260401 configs array; web_fetch also accepts max_content_tokens and web_search accepts user_location. Each configs entry is identified by its name and typed by an optional type, and requests that pass only name, enabled, and permission_policy continue to work; in the typed SDKs, configs entries become per-tool types. See Restrict web search and web fetch domains.
  • Claude Managed Agents sessions that run in a self-hosted sandbox can now attach memory stores. The Python, TypeScript, and Go SDK workers download each attached store into the sandbox at its mount_path and sync the agent’s changes back to the store. See Memory stores in self-hosted sandboxes.
  • The session viewer in the Claude Console has been redesigned with a timeline minimap, a transcript grouped by model request, and an Inspector panel for session details and cost, raw events, per-tool statistics, mounted resources, and per-thread activity. See Inspect a session in the Console.

item.title: Workbench is now playground in the Claude Console.
item.content:encoded: • Workbench is now playground in the Claude Console. Playground supports every Messages API parameter and includes templates that demonstrate API features such as code execution and web search. It shows the full SDK request and the API response for each run, to help you understand the API and build with it. For more, see the Claude Help Center or try it at platform.claude.com/playground.

item.title: The Compliance API now returns transcripts of Cowork and Cla…
item.description: Full title: The Compliance API now returns transcripts of Cowork and Claude Code sessions that run on your users’ machines, in beta for Claude Enterprise…
item.content:encoded:
• The Compliance API now returns transcripts of Cowork and Claude Code sessions that run on your users’ machines, in beta for Claude Enterprise organizations. GET /v1/compliance/apps/sessions/local lists sessions across your organization, GET /v1/compliance/apps/sessions/local/{session_id} retrieves one session’s metadata, and GET /v1/compliance/apps/sessions/local/{session_id}/messages returns its transcript, all with your existing Compliance Access Key and the read:compliance_user_data scope. See Sessions on users’ machines.
  • We’ve added the anthropic-workspace-id response header to the Claude API. It carries the wrkspc_-prefixed ID of the workspace that the request’s API key or access token resolved to, including your organization’s Default Workspace. See Identify the workspace behind an API response.

item.title: The introductory pricing for Claude Sonnet 5 ($2 / $10 USD p…
item.description: Full title: The introductory pricing for Claude Sonnet 5 ($2 / $10 USD per MTok) is now the standard price: the previously scheduled increase to $3 / $15…
item.content:encoded: • The introductory pricing for Claude Sonnet 5 ($2 / $10 USD per MTok) is now the standard price: the previously scheduled increase to $3 / $15 USD per MTok on September 1, 2026, will not occur. See Pricing.

item.title: You can now set a budget on a Claude Managed Agents session:…
item.description: Full title: You can now set a budget on a Claude Managed Agents session: a hard cap on the session’s spend, priced at public list rates.
item.content:encoded:
• You can now set a budget on a Claude Managed Agents session: a hard cap on the session’s spend, priced at public list rates. A session that reaches its budget pauses with the budget_reached stop reason instead of starting new model requests; changing or removing the budget resumes it. Deployments accept the same budget and apply it to each session they start. See Session budgets.
  • You can now give a Claude Managed Agents session an advisor: a model at least as capable as the agent’s own that the session’s primary thread can consult mid-turn for strategic guidance. Configure it as a {"type": "advisor"} entry in the agent’s multiagent roster, naming the model to consult. See Give the session an advisor.
  • You can now control where model inference runs for a Claude Managed Agents agent. Set inference_geo inside the model object when you create the agent (see Pin the inference geo), or override it for a single session. See Data residency for the available geos and pricing.
  • Claude Managed Agents sessions can now load skills from a GitHub repository. When a session mounts a repository, any skills in its root .claude/skills directory are discovered automatically at session start and available to the agent for that session.

item.title: Inference hooks are now in beta for Claude Enterprise organi…
item.description: Full title: Inference hooks are now in beta for Claude Enterprise organizations.
item.content:encoded:
• Inference hooks are now in beta for Claude Enterprise organizations. Point Claude at your organization’s AI security server, and each governed prompt across claude.ai, Cowork, and Claude Code is held for the server’s allow or deny verdict before inference proceeds. Requests are signed, failure handling is configurable, and every denial is recorded in the compliance Activity Feed. See Inference hooks.
  • We’ve retired the Claude Opus 4.1 model (claude-opus-4-1-20250805). All requests to this model on the Claude API will now return an error. We recommend upgrading to Claude Opus 5. Researchers can request ongoing access through the External Researcher Access Program.

item.title: The Compliance API now returns transcripts of Cowork session…
item.description: Full title: The Compliance API now returns transcripts of Cowork sessions started on claude.ai web or mobile, in beta for Claude Enterprise organizations.
item.content:encoded: • The Compliance API now returns transcripts of Cowork sessions started on claude.ai web or mobile, in beta for Claude Enterprise organizations. GET /v1/compliance/apps/sessions/remote lists sessions and GET /v1/compliance/apps/sessions/remote/{session_id}/messages returns one session’s transcript, using your existing Compliance Access Key with the read:compliance_user_data scope. See Sessions in the cloud.

item.title: Dreams (research preview) now supports Claude Opus 5.
item.content:encoded: • Dreams (research preview) now supports Claude Opus 5. See Supported models.

item.title: We’ve launched Claude Opus 5 (claude-opus-5), a step-change…
item.description: Full title: We’ve launched Claude Opus 5 (claude-opus-5), a step-change improvement over Claude Opus 4.8.
item.content:encoded:
• We’ve launched Claude Opus 5 (claude-opus-5), a step-change improvement over Claude Opus 4.8. Claude Opus 5 supports a 1M token context window (both the default and the maximum), 128k max output tokens, and thinking on by default, at $5 / $25 USD per MTok, the same pricing as Claude Opus 4.8. It’s available on the Claude API, Claude in Amazon Bedrock, Claude Platform on AWS, Claude Models on Google Cloud (Google managed), and Claude in Microsoft Foundry. See Claude Opus 5 and the models overview for complete specs.
  • On Claude Opus 5, disabling thinking is allowed only at effort high or below: thinking: {"type": "disabled"} with effort xhigh or max returns a 400 error, a breaking change from Claude Opus 4.8. See Effort with thinking.
  • Effort is the primary control for steering Claude Opus 5: the model supports the full ladder (low, medium, high, xhigh, max), with max for capability-critical work.
  • Mid-conversation tool changes are now in beta on Claude Fable 5, Claude Mythos 5, Claude Opus 4.8, and Claude Opus 5: add or remove tools between turns of a conversation while preserving the prompt cache. Include the mid-conversation-tool-changes-2026-07-01 beta header in your requests.
  • The fallbacks parameter now supports a "default" mode, which applies Anthropic’s recommended fallback models by refusal category. Server-side fallback is in beta, and the "default" mode requires the server-side-fallback-2026-07-01 beta header. See Refusals and fallback.
  • We’ve removed fast mode for Claude Opus 4.7. Requests to claude-opus-4-7 with speed: "fast" now return an error; unlike Claude Opus 4.6, they do not fall back to standard speed. Claude Opus 4.7 itself remains available at standard speed. To continue using fast mode, migrate to Claude Opus 5 or Claude Opus 4.8. Read more in Fast mode model availability.
